questions.q: What does a journal source identify?
options: The business purpose of the entry
Which balancing segment the journal affects
Which system or process created the journal
Whether the journal has been posted
questions.explain: Source identifies the origin — Manual, Payables, Allocation, and so on.

questions.q: What does a journal category identify?
options: The system that created the journal
The ledger the journal belongs to
The approval workflow stage
The business purpose of the entry, such as Accrual or Adjustment
questions.explain: Category describes why the journal exists — its business purpose.

questions.q: Can a single journal mix an Accrual line and a Reclassification line?
options: No, every line in a journal must share the same category
Yes, as long as debits equal credits
Only if the source is Manual
Only in a secondary ledger
questions.explain: All lines in a journal entry must share one category; mixed purposes require separate journals.

questions.q: Which source is generated automatically when subledger transactions are transferred to GL, rather than typed in by hand?
options: Manual
Payables
Spreadsheet
None — all journals start as Manual
questions.explain: Payables (and similarly Receivables, Fixed Assets) journals are generated by subledger accounting rules, not typed by hand.

questions.q: Why does the source/category combination matter beyond labeling?
options: It has no real functional impact
It only affects how a journal looks when printed
It determines the ledger's functional currency
Later features like approval rules and auto-post criteria sets commonly target specific source/category combinations
questions.explain: Approval rules, auto-post criteria, and suspense account rules are commonly scoped to specific source/category pairs.
